overturns can be detected from standard meteorological LR soundings but that they are not frequent and are rather rare in the free atmosphere.

the detection of overturning events from LR soundings is possible, but the probability of occurrence is very small, and therefore the detection of small-scale overturns is not possible.

the Thorpe analysis applied to standard radiosondes is a good method to detect overturns in the troposphere.

the Thorpe analysis of standard radiosonde profiles provides a useful tool to detect large-scale turbulent events in the tropo- spheric and stratospheric boundary layers, but it is less efficient for detecting small- scale turbulent overturns.

, although the probability of occurrence is small, overturns detected in radiosonde profiles are real events, and can be considered as reliable indicators of small-scale turbulence in the atmosphere.
